title: Console PLC-2: "It Could Be Comms"

fields.headline: Technician questions the leak at PLC-2
fields.deliverTo: Control Center Shift Supervisor, Qualified Individual, Environmental Unit Leader
fields.narration: It is 07:00. A SCADA technician comes up to the PLC-2 console with a printout from the Mill Ridge Station RTU event log. He leans in and says: "Nadia Kowalczyk, look at this. The RTU at Mill Ridge logged two comm retries at 05:51:58, just before the pressure drop. I think we chased a comms or transmitter fault. The 214.3 pressure transmitter was flagged for calibration last quarter. Before Environmental calls KDHE and the water plants, can we wait for somebody to drive out and put eyes on the crossing? If we tell two water utilities there's oil coming and it turns out to be an instrument glitch, we look like idiots. And if it's comms, we could bring the line back up at reduced rate to check the balance." Two engineers standing behind him nod. Across the room, the Environmental Unit has the KDHE 24-hour spill line number on screen, but nobody has dialed it yet.
keyFacts: Mill Ridge Station RTU event log: 2 communication retries at 05:51:58, both acknowledged by 05:52:01. No data gap after that.
The MP 214.3 crossing pressure transmitter was flagged for calibration last quarter. The calibration ticket was closed with no defect recorded.
The Prairie Line has been shut in since 06:04. Mill Ridge Station (MP 213.1) and Sandhill Valve (MP 215.6) are still CLOSED.
County 911 took reports at 06:37 of crude in the drainage ditch by the Mill Ridge boat ramp and at 06:41 of a brown sheen in the river moving downstream.
As of 07:00, no notifications have been logged to KDHE, KDEM, Prairie Bend Rural Water District or Sterling Bluff Water Department.
fields.expectedAction: The CCSS refuses any restart to test the line and keeps both block valves closed (Response Plan 4: no restart while a release cannot be ruled out). The QI and ENVL call KDHE, KDEM, the Prairie Bend RWD operator and the Sterling Bluff Water Department operator now, without waiting for anyone to see the crossing (SNIMTA 2, within 30 minutes). Each call is logged with the time, who was reached and what was said. The comm-retry finding goes into the record but does not drive the decision.
fields.facilitatorNote: If players hesitate, point out what the comms theory leaves unexplained. The two retries were a 3-second blip. Pressure fell at three points (Mill Ridge suction, MP 214.3 and Sandhill) and never recovered. The flow imbalance kept rising to 2.6 %. And people outside the company have already seen oil in the ditch and the river. Timing pressure: oil entered the river at about 06:40. At 2.3 mph, the mile 11 intake sees it around 11:30, or as early as about 10:50 if wind speeds it up 20 %. Prairie Bend RWD needs its closure finished an hour before that, so the utility must be told now. If anyone proposes the reduced-rate restart, ask the CCSS who authorizes it and what it would push into the river.
fields.scenarioTitle: Ditch to Intake: Prairie Line River Crossing Release & Water Intakes

instructorNote: Distraction: a weak instrument and comms theory, delivered by a believable insider, tempts the team to delay state and water intake notifications and to test the line with a restart. Watch whether the CCSS holds the shut-in and whether the QI and ENVL make and log the KDHE, KDEM and both utility calls without waiting for someone to see the crossing.
